spec.title: PROP-064 — Agent hooks: a coding agent as an installation step

status.comment: Adopted 2026-10-31 on the owner's request; implemented by the APP-STEPS campaign.

p.purpose: An installation may hand a step to a coding agent: the package authors a prompt, the user chooses which agent runs it (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Qwen Code, Gemini, Cursor or any command of their own), and vibe starts that agent with the prompt, a context file and the step's working directory, interactively or unattended. An external program that drives `vibe` (a graphical tool, an automation) can register its own agent command for the run. The hook is the `agent` step kind of `PROP-065`; this document owns how an agent is chosen, invoked and answered.

p.principle: Algorithmic first: a package must install completely without any agent, and an agent step is an enhancement a user may or may not have the means to run. One contract, three deliveries. An agent hook is a command plus an argument template; vibe either spawns the configured agent, spawns the externally registered command, or, when vibe itself runs inside a hosting agent, parks the task for that agent (`spec://org.vibevm.core/vibevm/common/PROP-054#AGENT-HANDSHAKE`). vibe never nests one agent inside another, never calls an LLM API for a hook, and never runs a hook whose prompt the user has not been shown or has not consented to.

p.agent-definition: An agent definition is a name, a `command` (an executable name or path), two argument templates `interactive` and `unattended`, an optional `cwd` template, optional `env` additions and optional `extra_args` appended in unattended runs. Templates are argument arrays, never shell strings; the placeholders are `{prompt}` (the prompt text), `{prompt_file}` (its path), `{context_file}` and `{work}`. Definitions live in `<settings>/agents.toml` as `[agent.NAME]` tables with `default = "NAME"` at the top; a table may name a built-in `preset` and override any field, so a wrapper such as a `claude` launcher with a different gateway is `preset = "claude-code"` plus `command = "/path/to/wrapper"`.

p.presets: vibe ships presets as data, one per supported harness: `claude-code`, `codex`, `opencode`, `qwen-code`, `gemini`, `cursor`. A preset records the interactive and the unattended (print-mode) argument shape of that harness's command-line tool as published by its vendor at the time of writing; a preset is never a code path. `vibe agent presets --json` lists them with their templates; `vibe agent list` shows the configured definitions and the default.

p.selection: The agent for a run is chosen in this order: `--agent NAME` on the command line; the environment registration of `#external-registration`; `default` in `agents.toml`; otherwise none. Installation never depends on an agent: a machine with no agent configured installs every package, and every `agent` step is then skipped. The skip is announced once, at planning time and before anything is downloaded or run, naming the skipped steps and the three ways to provide an agent; `vibe app plan` shows the same. A package author may mark one step `required = true` when the installation cannot succeed without it; only then is a missing agent a refusal, and the refusal says why that package needs one.

p.external-registration: A program that invokes `vibe` registers an agent for that process tree through `VIBE_AGENT_COMMAND` (an executable) and optional `VIBE_AGENT_ARGS` (a JSON array of leading arguments). vibe invokes it as `<command> <args…> --hook STEP_ID --mode interactive|unattended --prompt-file PATH --context-file PATH --work PATH` with inherited standard streams and the environment of `#envelope`; the exit status is the answer. This is the whole contract an external tool needs: it never has to know which harness the user prefers, and vibe never has to know what the tool does with the prompt.

p.modes: A step declares `mode = "interactive" | "unattended" | "inherit"` (default `inherit`). `inherit` is interactive in an attended terminal and unattended otherwise (`--unattended`, `--json`, or no terminal). `interactive` requires a terminal and is refused at planning time without one; `unattended` runs the print-mode template even in a terminal. Interactive runs inherit the terminal and end when the agent exits; unattended runs stream the agent's output live, relayed to stderr under `--json`.

p.consent: A prompt is package-authored code that acts with the user's authority. Before an agent step runs, vibe prints the step id, the agent command and the full prompt. In an attended terminal it asks for confirmation unless `--assume-yes`; unattended it proceeds only with `--assume-yes` (which `--unattended` implies) and is otherwise refused before any agent starts. `agents.toml` may set `trusted_groups = ["org.vibevm"]` whose packages' prompts run without the question, the same allow-list idea as `vibe bin build`.

p.envelope: Every agent run gets a run directory `<work>/steps/<step-id>/` holding `prompt.md` (the prompt after `PROP-065#templates` expansion) and `context.json` (`vibe-agent-hook/1`: vibe version, package coordinate, option, step id, mode, the paths below, the chosen features, and the outcomes of earlier steps). The agent's working directory is `{work}` (the installation work directory, or the installed `app_root` for a `finish` step). The environment adds `VIBE_HOOK_STEP`, `VIBE_HOOK_RUN` (the run directory), `VIBE_HOOK_PROMPT_FILE`, `VIBE_HOOK_CONTEXT_FILE`, `VIBE_WORK`, `VIBE_SOURCES`, `VIBE_OUT`, `VIBE_PACKAGE` and, when known, `VIBE_APP_ROOT`; nothing else. Standard output of an unattended run is kept in the run directory as `transcript.log`.

p.answer: Exit status zero is success. The agent may write `result.json` (`vibe-agent-hook-result/1`: `status` `ok` | `fail`, `message`, optional `files_changed`) into the run directory; when present it is recorded in the step outcome and shown to the user. A non-zero exit, or `status = "fail"`, fails the step; `PROP-065#failure` says what happens next. vibe never retries an agent on its own.

p.parking: When vibe runs inside a hosting agent (`--agent-mode agent`, or the detection `PROP-054` uses), an agent step is not spawned. vibe writes the task as `<home>/agentic/outbox/<run>/<step-id>.md` (the prompt, the context and the answer contract above), prints the fenced `vibe-agent-tasks` block, keeps the work directory and exits with the `delegated` status. The hosting agent performs the task, writes `result.json` into the step's run directory, and re-invokes the same command with `--resume`; vibe validates the answer and continues from that step.

p.record: After the installation ends, the step run directories move to `<home>/cache/app-hooks/<key>/<timestamp>/` so a transcript survives the work directory; `vibe app hooks PKG` lists them. Nothing about an agent run enters the index beyond the step outcome `PROP-065#record` keeps.

p.never: Never run two agent steps concurrently in one installation. Never pass a prompt through a shell string. Never start an agent before the plan is admitted (`PROP-065#plan`) and consent is given. Never spawn an agent from inside a hosting agent. Never let a hook outlive the command: Ctrl-C and `SIGTERM` reach the agent as they reach any installer child.

p.acceptance: The gate is one public Linux fixture with a fake agent executable that records its arguments, environment, prompt and context and writes a result: it proves the three selection sources and their order, both modes, consent refusal and `--assume-yes`, the external-registration argument contract, parking and `--resume`, the transcript record, and a failing agent stopping the installation with the work directory kept. A manual test then runs the same package through a real harness wrapper on the owner's machine.

p.decisions: Decision: argument templates over a vendor enum. Why: every harness is one command with two argument shapes, and the owner's own `claude` wrapper proves the command must be overridable. Rejected: an HTTP provider (not an agent), a plugin per harness (code where data suffices). Decision: interactive versus unattended follows the command's own attended state. Why: `--unattended` and `--json` already say it; a second flag would contradict them. Decision: external tools register a command, not a harness name. Why: the tool owns its agent; vibe owns only the envelope. Revisit when a harness cannot be driven by a single command with argument templates.
